title: Stalling host runloop lock contention — incident notes & temporary runbook
content:
Summary:
On 2025-01-14 between ~02:15–03:45 UTC we observed a class of request stalls on a subset of serving hosts in us-west-2. Symptoms were long tail latency and batch formation delays resulting in higher batching latency, sudden memory accumulation in worker processes, and eventual OOM kills on 6 hosts. The root cause appears to be a hot-path mutex in the host runloop that started contending under a change in the microbatch scheduling logic (recent rollout: batch-leader-election v2). The mutex hold-duration grew under a particular request mix (many short, parallel streams) causing stalled dequeue, batch buildup on other threads, and unbounded KV cache prefetching.

Why this doc exists (goal):
- Capture an on-call timeline and immediate mitigations used.
- Produce a small, usable temporary runbook for next on-call rotation.
- List experiments and follow-ups to prevent recurrence.

High-level impact:
- User-facing: interleaved elevated tail latency for generation endpoints (p99 -> 12s from 800ms), increased error rate (context timeouts) for ~30 minutes during window.
- Internal: 6 hosts OOMed, autoscaler replaced them; requests spilled to dedicated/backup pool causing reduced capacity and throttling for some customers.

Timeline (concise):
- 02:10 UTC: Synthetic p99 alerts triggered for serving-route:/v1/generate in us-west-2.
- 02:12 UTC: Pager oncall (Aisha) acknowledged, opened Slack thread. Initial triage: traces show long wait-before-first-token and mem+CPU stable on aggregate.
- 02:18 UTC: SRE traces show a cluster of hosts with very high syscall latency in per-host flamegraphs; top call is runloop::main_mutex -> schedule_microbatch.
- 02:25 UTC: Confirmed that microbatching rollout v2 (canary 20%) released prior day to canary ring including these hosts (JIRA-INF-2028).
- 02:30 UTC: Manual rollback of batch-leader-election v2 to v1 on affected ASG; immediate reduction in new incidents but two hosts already had runaway memory and were OOM-killed at 02:42/02:49.
- 03:05 UTC: Temporary dynconfig applied to limit prefetch concurrency per-tenant to 2. Latency normalized over next ~20–30m.
- 03:45 UTC: Incident marked as contained. Full post-incident follow-up scheduled.

Signal analysis (what we saw):
- Flamegraphs/cpu: top spike at runloop mutex held in schedule path; hold times increased from ~200 us -> 15–40 ms under load mix.
- Traces: multiple traces show wait-on-lock spans correlating with long delay before microbatch dispatch.
- Memory: KV prefetch goroutines accumulated entries while dequeue path stalled; resident memory rose linearly until OOM.
- Kernel: dmesg showed oom-killer invoked on affected processes; no host-level pressure prior to the runaway.
- Telemetry: batch formation size distribution shifted (more tiny batches queued), queue length histograms spiked.

Immediate mitigations performed (ordered):
1) Rollback batch-leader-election v2 to previous config on canary ASG (hotfix). Effect: drop in new occurrences within ~3–5m.
2) Apply dynconfig: prefetch.max-concurrency=2 (global temporary override). Effect: prevented new runaway memory growth.
3) Increase watchdog OOM threshold timer (short term) to avoid noisy restarts during rollback window.
4) Evacuate two hosts showing >90% of KV allocations to replacement hosts via ASG termination (to avoid cascading network-side saturation).
5) Add temporary alert for lock-hold-duration > 5ms on runloop mutex.

Root cause hypothesis (current):
- A change in the microbatch scheduling logic introduced a small critical section that now performs a synchronous lookup/acquire of a per-request resource while holding the runloop mutex. Under pathological mixes (many concurrent short streams), the critical section experiences head-of-line blocking. That blocking delays dequeue/dispatch; meanwhile prefetching logic keeps spawning goroutines that allocate KV cache entries without backpressure because the token that would throttle them was stuck behind the same mutex. Result: memory accumulation and OOM.

Why cache-prefetch interacted badly:
- Prefetch routine assumed dequeue path would make forward progress and relied on a token to be consumed quickly. When progress stalled the prefetch queue grew unbounded.

Temporary runbook (for next 48–72h while we validate fixes):
- Pager steps (SRE oncall):
  1) Confirm p99 latency alert and isolate affected AZ/ASG using per-host p99 dashboard.
  2) Run quick diagnostic: ssh into host, collect top 30 stack traces of serving process (sample every 200ms for 10s) and run 'pstack' (or go tool pprof) to confirm runloop mutex is hot.
  3) If runloop mutex hold-time > 5ms and KV prefetch queue length > threshold: apply dynconfig prefetch.max-concurrency=2 and set batch-backoff=true.
  4) If >2 hosts show runaway memory: initiate ASG replacement for those hosts (terminate instance to force immediate replacement) and mark them in incident doc.
  5) Rollback microbatching rollout in the ring where the failure is observed (canary -> full rollout aborted).

Debug commands and quick checks (notes for oncall):
- ps aux | grep serving_process; pid=$(...)
- sudo gdb -p $pid --batch -ex "thread apply all bt" > /tmp/backtrace.txt
- go tool pprof -http=:6060 http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=10
- sudo perf record -p $pid -g -- sleep 10; sudo perf script | flamegraph.pl > /tmp/flame.svg
- curl "{{metrics}}/api/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runloop_lock_hold_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, host))"

Unresolved questions / things to validate:
- Was the prefetch token supposed to be consumed from a different queue? Need code audit to confirm. (Assigned: Mateo)
- Is there a safer way to limit prefetch work without holding the runloop lock? Could we move the synchronous lookup outside the critical section? (Assigned: Jin)
- Why did only a subset of hosts hit the worst-case? Investigate host-configuration drift (kernel version, CPU steal, runtime sched tuning). (Assigned: Evelyn)

Follow-up action items (owner & ETA):
- Short-term code rollback or patch to reduce lock scope (Jin) — target: 2025-01-21.
- Add backpressure in prefetch path (Mateo) — target: 2025-01-28.
- Add eBPF tracing job to capture lock-hold histograms per host for next 7 days (SRE infra) — target: 2025-01-20.
- Expand canary testing with synthetic short-stream workload to surface this regression (product/QA) — target: 2025-02-04.

Notes to reviewers / context for the team:
- This incident is an example of a behavioral regression where a small sync change amplified under a workload pattern we didn't simulate in canary. The fix is likely small (reduce scope), but we must harden prefetch/backpressure assumptions and improve canary workloads to include high fan-in, short-lived streams.

Links / references:
- Incident ticket: JIRA-INF-2028
- Slack thread: https://redwood.slack.com/archives/C1SRE/p1671234567000
- Candidate patch PR: https://github.com/redwood/repo/pull/987

Appendix: short checklist to paste into pager message (copy/paste):
- "If you see p99 > 5s and runloop_lock_hold_sec P50 > 5ms: 1) set prefetch.max-concurrency=2, 2) rollback batch-leader-election rollout in that ring, 3) replace hosts with runaway mem. Notify eng-serving-runtime and product-hosted-api."

End of notes.
